clue.text: Have one's back to the wall, with partly circumscribed view of sea

definitions.text: Have one's back to the wall

explanation.surface: Someone cornered against a wall, gazing out over an enclosed stretch of sea.
explanation.walkthrough: A bay is sea partly enclosed by land, so a stand (viewpoint) at one gives a partly circumscribed view of sea; 'with' joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cornered and forced to face attackers is the first sense; the second reads the phrase literally as a viewing place on an inlet, water almost enclosed by land.

clue.text: It carried two out of. three 'on the bummel

definitions.text: It carried two out of. three 'on the bummel

parts.words: It carried two out of. three 'on the bummel
parts.note: in Jerome K Jerome's Three Men on the Bummel the friends cycle through Germany, two of them sharing a bicycle made for a pair

explanation.surface: A reference to a vehicle in a comic travel book about three men on a German tour.
explanation.walkthrough: Three Men on the Bummel (1900) is Jerome K Jerome's sequel to Three Men in a Boat; two of the three ride a two-seater bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bicycle with two seats one behind the other carries two riders.

clue.text: "There's a divinity" that shares its function

definitions.text: "There's a divinity" that shares its function

parts.words: "There's a divinity" that shares its function
parts.note: Hamlet's line runs 'There's a divinity that shapes our ends'; the tool here also shapes ends, those of fingers

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean god compared with something that does the same job.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation continues 'that shapes our ends' (Hamlet); a manicure tool shapes the ends of the fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: An emery board or metal rasp is used to shape the tips of fingernails.

clue.text: What a card! The pride of Fall Mall?

explanation.surface: Admiration for a witty character, and the glory of a famous London street.
explanation.walkthrough: Pall Mall is a London street lined with gentlemen's clubs, so the finest club is its pride.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest-ranking card in the club suit; and Pall Mall, the London street of gentlemen's clubs, would claim the best club as its pride.

clue.text: Guns that help lighten the battle ?

definitions.text: Guns that help lighten the battle

parts.words: Guns that help lighten the battle
parts.note: a group of artillery pieces lights up a battlefield with its flashes, and an electric cell lights a torch

explanation.surface: Artillery whose firing lights up a battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of artillery guns is a battery, and so is a cell that powers a lamp.

clue.text: Key to American learning ?

explanation.surface: The secret of education in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: A cylinder lock key takes its name from its inventor Linus Yale; and an Ivy League university in Connecticut bears the same name.

clue.text: Most of the egg is blue — somehow this is charming

indicators.note: 'somehow' says the letters are arranged in some unstated way, signalling an anagram
most of the word means all but its final letter is kept

parts.note: the egg gives the word egg

explanation.surface: An egg that is mostly blue is somehow delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' trims EGG to EG; 'somehow' rearranges EG + IS + BLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To beguile is to charm or enchant someone.

clue.text: It's sapped, but there 'must be some coal left ?

explanation.surface: A weakened structure beside a mine with reserves still unmined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But' joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Weakened from beneath is the first sense; read as 'under-mined', a seam not fully worked would still hold coal.

clue.text: Like the bird in our wake

parts.note: 'like' can mean 'as', in the same way as
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A seabird following behind a ship, trailing in its wake.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'like the bird' as a simile about a gull trailing a ship; the definition is the position behind the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something behind a moving vessel lies in its wake, towards the rear of the ship.

clue.text: Where's Spanish Hero's dinner? Ten misrepresented what happened

parts.note: once eaten, the Spanish hero El Cid's dinner is inside him: in Cid

indicators.note: to misrepresent is to present wrongly, so these three letters are given in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about a Spanish hero's meal, then a muddled account of events.
explanation.walkthrough: The question is answered 'in Cid': El Cid is the Spanish national hero and his dinner is in his stomach. 'Misrepresented' rearranges TEN into ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An incident is an event, a thing that occurred.

clue.text: Valued servant-girl found to belong to the Crown ?

definitions.text: found to belong to the Crown

explanation.surface: A much-prized maid is discovered to be royal property.
explanation.walkthrough: Treasure trove was valuables found buried with no known owner, which in Britain went to the Crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A prized domestic helper is called a gem; and in English law gold or silver hoards dug up were declared trove owned by the monarch.

clue.text: One thousand good warriors ?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for good

explanation.surface: A count of a thousand worthy fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: An impi is a Zulu regiment, a body of warriors.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi was a Zulu fighting regiment, so a band of armed men.

clue.text: One way to pass secrets in some galleries ?

definitions.text: One way to pass secrets in some galleries

parts.words: One way to pass secrets in some galleries
parts.note: in a whispering gallery, such as the one in St Paul's Cathedral, soft speech carries round the dome

explanation.surface: How confidences might be passed on in an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: A whispering gallery (as in St Paul's Cathedral, London) carries murmured words across the dome.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking very softly, under one's breath, is how secrets are passed and how such galleries work.

clue.text: The course of learning

parts.note: read plainly, a programme of school or university study; the Latin word behind it means a race or a racecourse

explanation.surface: A plain description of a school syllabus.
explanation.definitionFit: A school's programme of subjects is its syllabus, and the Latin original means a running track.

clue.text: Not separated, you say? That's unwise

indicators.note: 'you say' marks a word spoken aloud and matched by its sound

parts.note: indiscrete means not divided into distinct parts

explanation.surface: Someone asks if things are joined, then calls that unwise.
explanation.walkthrough: INDISCRETE (not separate) and INDISCREET (unwise) sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: An indiscreet act is careless or tactless, lacking good judgement.

clue.text: Drink, somewhat sticky or sweet

parts.note: wine is an alcoholic drink
gum is a sticky substance, an adhesive

explanation.surface: A drink described as rather sticky or sugary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' is the definition: in Britain a sweet is a piece of confectionery, and a wine gum is a chewy fruit sweet that contains no wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine gum is a chewy British confection, a type of candy.

clue.text: No Latin a different subject

indicators.note: 'different' means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A student dropping Latin for a different school subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject' is not a school subject but a citizen of a country; 'different' rearranges NO LATIN A.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of a country, one of its people, is a national.

clue.text: To sum up, one child and an essayist

parts.note: to sum figures up is to add them
I is the Roman numeral for one
a son is a child

explanation.surface: Arithmetic with a single child, then a writer of essays.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Addison was the 18th-century English essayist of The Spectator.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Addison co-founded The Spectator and is famed for his prose pieces.

clue.text: Overlord's job

parts.note: Operation Overlord was the codename for the Allied landings in Normandy in 1944

explanation.surface: The duty of a feudal lord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overlord' looks like a lord's duties, but it is the 1944 D-Day operation, whose task was an attack on occupied France.
explanation.definitionFit: Operation Overlord's purpose was to land forces in enemy-held France, an armed incursion.

clue.text: No gentleman, the Scot from Nova Scotia

parts.note: a cad is no gentleman, so the phrase gives 'a cad'
Ian is a typical Scottish name

explanation.surface: A Scotsman from Nova Scotia who behaves badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Acadia was the French name for the region including Nova Scotia.
explanation.definitionFit: Acadia was the old French colony covering Nova Scotia, so its people and things are Acadian.

clue.text: Cuts across between the parties

parts.note: inter- is a prefix meaning between
sects are factions or parties

explanation.surface: Something that slices across the divide between political parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines that cross each other meet and divide at a point, which is what intersecting means.

clue.text: Space with nothing inside, ..see ?

indicators.note: the zero letter goes within the abbreviation for see, as 'inside' places one piece in another

parts.note: VID is short for vide, Latin for see, used in references
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An empty space, with the reader told to look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' puts O within VID, the abbreviation of Latin vide (see).
explanation.definitionFit: A void is an empty space, a vacuum.

clue.text: Country title Jacob won

explanation.surface: A country whose name Jacob earned.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis 32 Jacob is renamed after wrestling through the night.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle Eastern nation; and in Genesis Jacob wrestled an angel and was given the name meaning 'he strives with God'.

clue.text: Failed in exam at Cirencester ?

parts.note: old student slang for flunking, which suits Cirencester, home of the Royal Agricultural College where farming is taught

explanation.surface: A student failing an examination at the Cirencester college.
explanation.walkthrough: Cirencester is an English town with an agricultural college, so farming students who fail are aptly said to have tilled the field.
explanation.definitionFit: In old British university slang a candidate who failed an examination was said to have been ploughed.

clue.text: Owns a piano that's done up

parts.note: to own something is to have it
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Someone owns a renovated piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Done up' looks like renovated, but it means fastened.
explanation.definitionFit: A hasp is a hinged metal clasp used to fasten a door or lid.

clue.text: Wrecked Claire in Pacific

indicators.note: something wrecked is smashed up, so these letters are broken and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A girl called Claire shipwrecked in the Pacific Ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pacific' looks like the ocean but means peaceable; 'Wrecked' rearranges CLAIRE IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Irenical means promoting peace, from the Greek for peace, so peaceable.

clue.text: Responds concerning the follower of the gospels

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the Acts of the Apostles is the New Testament book that comes after the four gospels

explanation.surface: Someone replies about a disciple of the gospels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follower' suggests a disciple, but it is the book that follows the gospels in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: To react is to respond to a stimulus.

clue.text: Title--" Penny Change: or How the Prodigal Returned "

indicators.note: change here means alter the order, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mock book title about a penny and the parable of the prodigal son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' rearranges TITLE and PENNY; the prodigal son of the parable came home sorry for his ways.
explanation.definitionFit: The prodigal son came home in remorse, contritely seeking his father's forgiveness.
